newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas up in Q4, slips in Q1, volume "not bad".
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas up in Q4, slips in Q1, volume "not bad".

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract saw 90 lots traded on Thursday morning in seven separate deals, with trade centred on the fourth quarter and in Q1 98.
All three months in the fourth quarter traded up from Wednesday's settlement price, while January and February slipped slightly but with only a single trade done in each month.
A futures broker pointed out that on the physical market, the prompt period remains the most active and this may reflect on the May futures contract, the current front month.
"There's certainly some prompt business going through and it might get active in May," he said, pointing out that the May contract expires next Tuesday.

The futures screen is still following the physical market closely, he said. "It's now following the OTC more than anything. The screen lags behind the OTC at the moment," he added, saying that players look first at the physical market and will only trade futures if there is a price advantage over the OTC market for doing so.

The recent reduction of margin calls is seen as a possible incentive for smaller shippers to enter the futures market, but so far the number of players actively and regularly involved in the market remains disappointing, he said.
But the volume of trade on Thursday morning, 90 lots, was described as "not bad", and is more than in some recent two-hour morning sessions.
